# Exam - Introduction to Machine Learning

The goal of this exam is to perform an analysis on data related to heart disease.
We would like to explore the relationship between a `target` variable - whether a patient has a heart disease or not - and several other variables such as cholesterol level, age, ...

The dataset is stored in the file `'heartData_simplified.csv'`, which is a cleaned and simplified version of the [UCI heart disease data set](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/datasets/heart+Disease).

You should explore the dataset and answer the questions of the exam in an R notebook, with comments explaining what you did.
You should send your code to **wandrille.duchemin [at] unibas.ch**.
Please name the file in an easily-identifiable way (eg exam_JohnSMITH.Rmd)!

## Description of the columns

-   age: Patient age in years.
-   sex: Patient sex (amle/female).
-   chol: Cholesterol level in mg/dl.
-   thalach: Maxium heart rate during the stress test.
-   oldpeak: Decrease of the ST segment during exercise relative to the same one during rest.
-   ca: Number of main blood vessels coloured by the radioactive dye. The number varies between 0 and 3.
-   thal: Results of the blood flow observed via the radioactive dye.
    -   defect -\> fixed defect (no blood flow in some part of the heart)
    -   normal -\> normal blood flow
    -   reversible -\> reversible defect (abnormal blood flow)
-   target: Whether the patient has a heart disease or not.

**Code to read the data**

```{r}
library(dplyr)

df = read.csv( "heartData_simplified.csv" )
df %>% head()
```

```{r}
dim(df)
```


## Instructions

Your mission is to implement a machine learning pipeline in order to predict `target`.

Try to choose a relevant approach regarding :

-   the split of your data into train and test sets
-   the metric you would like to optimize
-   the preprocessing steps you want to take

Try a logistic regression and a decision tree approach.

-   Which one yields the best result here ?
-   If you had to remove 3 features (*i.e.*, columns) out of this analysis, which ones would you choose ?
-   Try to describe briefly (in 3 or 4 sentences) which insights your model gives you about the relationship between heart disease and the covariables.

**important notes:**

-   it is a good idea to start with some data exploration.
-   You can see that we have several categorical variables in the dataset: `sex` , `thal`, and our response variable : `target`. If taken as-is, these variables may create problems in ML models. So you may first need to transform them somehow into numerical columns (there is a recipe step for this).
